title: Flow Problem Detected
shortDescription: Hot Spring spa detects insufficient water flow through heater.
fullDescription:
FL means flow through the heater is lower than required for safe operation. Hot Spring uses a pressure switch on most Highlife and Limelight models.

Dirty filters are the #1 cause. A partly closed slice valve, airlock, or failed pressure switch come next.

fixSteps.title: Open slice valves
fixSteps.instruction: Under access panel, verify gate valves above heater are fully open.

whenToCallPro: Circulation pump (SilentFlo) replacement needs a tech.
videoSearchQuery: Hot Spring spa FL flow error fix

faq.a: No — it's a safety shutdown to protect the heater.

title: Flow Switch Stuck Closed
shortDescription: Flow detector reports flow when the circulation pump is off.
fullDescription:
FLC appears when the flow switch reads 'flowing' even with the pump off. Scale or stuck paddle holds the switch closed.

Replacement of the pressure switch resolves most FLC cases.

fixSteps.title: Replace switch
fixSteps.instruction: With spa off, remove pressure switch and install new one.

videoSearchQuery: Hot Spring FLC flow closed switch

faq.a: Yes — just failing in the opposite direction.

title: Water Overheat
shortDescription: Water exceeded 110°F — spa shut down and cools before restarting.
fullDescription:
OH on Hot Spring spas indicates temperature reached 110°F or higher. The control disables heating until water drops to a safe level.

Excessive filter cycle times and stuck heater relays are the usual culprits. Remove cover to speed cooling.

fixSteps.title: Open cover to cool
fixSteps.instruction: Remove cover; spa resumes when water is safe.

whenToCallPro: Repeated OH with normal use — board service.

faq.a: Not until water cools and OH clears.

title: Temperature Sensor Fault
shortDescription: Spa temperature sensor is reading out of range.
fullDescription:
SN covers both high-limit and regulation sensors on Hot Spring IQ2020 boards. The display sometimes distinguishes with a suffix.

Confirm sensor is seated in the heater sensor port, then test resistance. Replace with the correct Hot Spring sensor.

fixSteps.title: Reseat sensor
fixSteps.instruction: Open service panel, unplug and reseat sensor on IQ2020 board.

whenToCallPro: If sensor is seized in heater, call tech.

faq.a: Use Hot Spring 73606 or correct OEM — aftermarket may not match curve.

title: High Limit Trip
shortDescription: High limit sensor detected an over-temp condition and cut power to heater.
fullDescription:
HL is a latching trip — the spa won't heat until you acknowledge and reset. Caused by scale, low flow, or failed sensors.

Hot Spring usually requires cycling power to reset HL after root cause is fixed.

title: Dry Fire Warning
shortDescription: Heater may be running with no water inside — protective shutdown.
fullDescription:
dr (dry) indicates the heater tube may be empty. Happens most often post-refill when air is trapped.

Purge air and refill to proper level; code should clear within one circulation cycle.

fixSteps.title: Purge air
fixSteps.instruction: Fill through filter well to eliminate airlock; run jets briefly.

videoSearchQuery: Hot Spring dr dry fire fix

faq.a: Always fill through the filter compartment to reduce airlocks.

title: Pump Overload
shortDescription: Pump motor drew too much current and was shut down.
fullDescription:
OE indicates a pump tripped its overcurrent protection. A stuck Moto-Massage or jet pump is typical on older Hot Spring spas.

Clear debris and power cycle. Repeat OE likely means pump replacement.

faq.a: Only affected pump is disabled — others may still run.

title: Water Below Setpoint
shortDescription: Water is noticeably below setpoint — informational.
fullDescription: COO indicates water is more than 20°F below set temp. Normal after refill or long outage. Heater continues running until setpoint reached.

fixSteps.title: Wait for heat-up
fixSteps.instruction: Allow several hours for heater to reach setpoint.

whenToCallPro: If COO persists 24 hours, heater not working.

title: Ice / Freeze Protection
shortDescription: Very cold conditions — freeze protection is active.
fullDescription:
Hot Spring runs circulation pump at longer intervals when ICE appears. This protects plumbing from freezing.

Confirm equipment compartment is not exposed to severe cold. Add insulation if necessary.

fixSteps.title: Add insulation
fixSteps.instruction: Ensure cabinet doors are closed and any insulation is intact.

whenToCallPro: If ICE appears in warm weather.

faq.a: Yes — and jets cycle to keep lines from freezing.

title: No Water Detected
shortDescription: Control detected no water flow at all — similar to FL but persistent.
fullDescription: NO H2O means no water movement detected for an extended period. Could be a totally failed circulation pump or closed slice valves blocking the heater loop.

faq.a: No — spa will not heat and heater could be damaged.
